scaling_argument_10x.summary: Horizontal replication (stateless, read-only indices) absorbs a 10x QPS increase at roughly fixed per-request latency, as long as corpus size is fixed -- each replica just needs its own full index copy. The first thing to break under a SIMULTANEOUS 10x QPS + 10x corpus-size increase is per-replica index memory (this sandbox's own IVF ANN fallback, used because faiss was not installable here, is the specific compute bottleneck at that scale, since it loops per-query in Python rather than batching like FAISS's C++ implementation does). GBDT reranking batches cheaply and is not expected to be the limiting stage. See this module's own docstring for the full reasoning this summary is drawn from.
